## Act 1 · The promise (3:00)

*(On the title.)*
Good morning! The video was the quick version. Now I'll tell you the real one.
A few weeks ago I wanted to make a party game for our class: the Cumorah Academy Party. And I had no time.

### 2 · A chatbot talks. An agent does.
`[CLICK]`
First I asked a chatbot. It gave me good advice: ideas, rules, tips. But the work was still mine.
`[CLICK]`
Then I gave the same goal to an agent. And the agent didn't give me advice: it planned the game, wrote the code, tested it and fixed its own mistakes.
That's the whole class in one sentence: **a chatbot answers; an agent acts.**

### 3 · Agent = DJ. Tools = tracks.
`[CLICK]`
The easiest way to picture it: a DJ. A DJ doesn't play every instrument; they choose which track to use and when.
The agent is the same, and its tracks are its tools:
`[CLICK]` search the web,
`[CLICK]` check a calendar,
`[CLICK]` send an email,
`[CLICK]` write and run code.

> *Nota:* Cada clic sube un fader y añade una capa real a la música. Deja que se escuche un segundo: la clase *oye* la metáfora.

---

## Act 2 · Behind the scenes (6:00)

### 4 · Inside an agent
`[CLICK]` *(the camera flies into the 3D world; let it land)*
Let me show you what happened inside the agent while it built my game. In the middle is its brain, the AI model. Around it, a loop that never stops.

### 5 · The loop
`[CLICK]` *(the loop seen from above)* Four steps, again and again.
`[CLICK]` **Goal.** What I asked for: a party game for my class.
`[CLICK]` **Plan.** It split it up: rules, screens, scores.
`[CLICK]` **Act.** It wrote the code, for real.
`[CLICK]` **Check.** It ran the tests. If something failed, back to Plan.
Goal, plan, act, check. *(point at the moving light)* Until it's done.

> *Nota:* La cámara viaja a cada paso con cada clic. Deja que llegue antes de hablar.

### 6 · Tools are its hands
`[CLICK]`
To act, it needs hands. These are its tools:
`[CLICK]` Search, `[CLICK]` Calendar, `[CLICK]` Email, `[CLICK]` Files, `[CLICK]` Code.
An agent is only as useful as the tools you give it, and only as safe as the permissions you give it.

### 7 · Memory keeps the context
`[CLICK]`
And it remembered things:
`[CLICK]` **who I am,** and who my class is;
`[CLICK]` **the history,** what it had already tried and what failed;
`[CLICK]` **my preferences:** simple, colorful, for 20 people at once.
That's why every round turned out better.

## Act 3 · The twist + your turn (11:00)

### 8 · Done ✓ … but was it right?
`[CLICK]`
And then it told me: **"Done. Tests: 12 out of 12 passing."** *(pause)*
`[CLICK]` *(the music stops)*
I tried it in class. Twenty students joined at the same time… and the game froze. *(pause)*
The tests only checked a single player. The agent did its job, but it didn't know what I knew: that in my class we play twenty at once.
`[CLICK]`
**You test. You decide.** I told it what happened, it fixed it, and that time it did work. The agent runs the loop; you decide when it's good.

> *Nota:* Este es el corazón de la clase. Silencio real después de "the game froze". Cuenta el error con humor: le pasa a cualquiera.

### 9 · Chatbot or agent?
`[CLICK]`
Now you decide. I'll read a request: one hand if a chatbot is enough, both hands if you need an agent.
"Explain photosynthesis." *(hands)*
`[CLICK]` Chatbot! It's just information.
`[CLICK]` "Book my dentist appointment." *(hands)*
`[CLICK]` Agent! It has to check your calendar, use the dentist's website and confirm.
`[CLICK]` "Fix my code and test it." *(hands)*
`[CLICK]` Agent! And now you know what to do when it says "Done": test it.

> *Nota:* Deja 5–10 segundos por pregunta. Si alguien se equivoca, pregúntale por qué.

## Act 4 · You decide (14:00)

### 10 · Agents in everyday life
`[CLICK]`
This isn't only for code. Where could you use it?
`[CLICK]` **Plan a trip.** `[CLICK]` **Sort my inbox.** `[CLICK]` **Research homework,** with the sources so you can check them. `[CLICK]` **Build a game,** like mine.
What would you give it? *(ask 1–2 students and apply "goal, plan, act, check" to their example)*

### 11 · You stay in charge
`[CLICK]`
So, how do you stay in charge? Three rules:
`[CLICK]` **Give a clear goal.** "Help me" is a bad goal. "A game for 20 people, playable on phones" is a good one.
`[CLICK]` **Check the work.** "Done" doesn't mean "right". You saw it.
`[CLICK]` **Protect private data.** Never give it passwords, bank details or anything it doesn't need. Give it the smallest permissions that work.

### 12 · You are the DJ
`[CLICK]` *(the music comes back at full volume; let it play two seconds)*
The video asked: who decides? *(pause)*
The agent mixes the tracks and runs the loop. But you choose the music: you set the goal and you check the result.
**You are the DJ.**
